- When sentiment is positive (≥0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high for next 3–7 days.
- If history shows strong downward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive drops), model frequently underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for next 5–10 days.
- When sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.0), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 3–7 days.
- Model tends to lag in early periods (e.g., first 5–7 days of forecast horizon); adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% for first 5 days if history shows recent volatility.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., price drops after peak), model often holds too high; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates early in the horizon (first 10 days); apply downward correction of 0.5–1.5% for first 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
